name: Off-Road Vehicle
description: A vehicle not registered for the street, used for recreation on nonhighway roads, trails or other natural terrain, motorcycles included; an electric dirt bike like a Sur-Ron or Talaria ridden off-road is one.

restrictions.rule: Not registered for street use, and used recreationally on nonhighway roads, trails or natural terrain; no limit on motor power or speed (Revised Code of Washington §46.04.365)
Needs an ORV registration and decal from the Department of Licensing, except on agricultural or timber land the owner or operator's employer controls (Revised Code of Washington §46.09.420)
Every rider must wear a fastened motorcycle helmet on a nonhighway road, except an operator on their own land (Revised Code of Washington §46.09.470)
Needs adequate brakes, and a headlight and taillight from dusk to dawn on land the rider doesn't own (Revised Code of Washington §46.09.470)
Allowed on a nonhighway road, and parking areas serving ORV areas, only where the managing authority allows ORVs (Revised Code of Washington §46.09.450)

Allowed on a street, road or highway only where a city under 3,000 people or a county designates it by ordinance; there it's exempt from street registration and equipment rules (Revised Code of Washington §§46.09.360, 46.09.450)

Not allowed on trails or roads restricted to pedestrian or animal travel, on road shoulders or medians, in ways that damage soil or vegetation, or on a private nonhighway road the owner hasn't opened to ORVs (Revised Code of Washington §§46.09.450, 46.09.470)
Cities, counties and state agencies may regulate it on land and roads they control, but no less strictly than state law (Revised Code of Washington §46.09.360)
